correctness.rationale: The criterion with (t,0,t) gives f(0) ≤ f(t); with (s,0,t) and s ≤ t it then gives f(s) ≤ f(t). For c=a∨b, a△c ≤ b and f(a) ≤ f(c) give f(c) ≤ f(a)∨f(b); the reverse follows by monotonicity. Conversely x△y ≤ z is equivalent to x ≤ y∨z and y ≤ x∨z, so join preservation gives both output inequalities and hence the output difference bound. No finiteness or normality is needed. On an n-atom algebra each output bit is constant one or the OR of a freely chosen subset of input atoms; the latter choices give exactly the normal maps, confirming both counts and the tabulation. In the published Example 2.2, x={1}, y={1,3}, z={3} yields input difference {3} but output difference {2,3} not contained in f(z)={3}. This refutes the claimed bound, not the sufficiency implication for CEP or CEP itself.
residual_risks: The packaged scalar census is recorded finite corroboration, not an independent replay or the proof of the arbitrary-algebra result.
The review does not decide the example’s CEP by an alternative proof or reassess the paper’s other theorems.
